name: Jiang Xuefei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Jiang Xuefei is the chairman of Shenzhen Suntak Circuit Technology, one of China's largest makers of printed circuit boards.
He founded the company in May 1995 and also serves as its CEO.
Jiang holds an EMBA from Xiamen University.

name: Hideyuki Busujima
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Hideyuki Busujima is the son of Sankyo founder Kunio Busujima, who died in October 2016.
In 2023, Hideyuki stepped down as CEO of pachinko-machine maker Sankyo, but remains chairman.
Kunio transferred his shares of publicly-traded Sankyo to Hideyuki in 2014.
In 2020, Hideyuki sold 20 million shares back to the company, which cancelled them.

name: Fritz Draexlmaier
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Fritz Draexlmaier's eponymous auto parts maker counts among its customers Audi, BMW, Cadillac, Land Rover, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche and Tesla.
Founded by his parents, Draexlmaier Group began in 1958 with an order for wiring harnesses for the Goggomobil, a microcar produced by Hans Glas GmbH.
A company speciality, wiring harnesses run throughout the entire vehicle connecting electrical components and relaying data and electrical power.
It has diversified into the manufacture of electronic components, consoles, door and instrument panels and exclusive interiors for specific model
Although he stepped down as CEO in early 2019, Fritz continues to serve as chairman and shareholder representative.
Draexlmaier has more than 65,000 employees and 60 business sites across 20 countries.
forbes_facts: Fritz is an only child. His father, Fritz Sr., died in 1995 at age 80, and his mom, Lisa, died in 2018 at age 100.
In 2017, Draexlmaier Group opened its first U.S. manufacturing site in Livermore, California, with 230 employees.

name: Oscar Baeza Fares
forbes_bio: Oscar Eugenio Baeza Fares is the managing director and controlling shareholder of Mexican industrial food conglomerate, Grupo Bafar.
Baeza controls about 56% of the company's shares, while family members hold an additional 29% of the shares.
Baeza studied business at the Universty of Las Cruces in New Mexico and Harvard Business School.
Grupo Bafar had net sales of more than $450 million in 2024.

name: Zhou Guohui
appears_on: Forbes annual (2015-2017); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)

name: Grant Petty
forbes_bio: Grant Petty cofounded film industry hardware and software company Blackmagic Design in his garage in Melbourne, Australia in 2001.
Blackmagic Design's professional cinema cameras, electronic equipment and software known as DaVinci Resolve are used by Hollywood studios and YouTubers.
During the pandemic, Blackmagic profits soared tenfold to $115 million, as networks bought its low-cost gear to accommodate work-from-home.
Petty, who grew up poor, writes the code for all of Blackmagic's internal processes and stars in hour-long instructional videos for company products.

name: Qiu Zixin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun China (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: Qiu Zixin chairs Beijing Wantai Biological Pharmacy, a supplier of diagnostic tests for the healthcare industry.
China beverage industry titan Zhong Shanshan holds a stake in Beijing Wantai.

name: Wong Chun Hong
forbes_bio: Wong Chun Hong chairs Hong Kong-listed real estate company Top Spring International Holdings.
Wong is also the vice chairman of China-listed Rainbow Department Store.

name: Maria Pinheiro
forbes_bio: New to the Forbes Billionaires List in 2021, Maria Barros Pinheiro is the cofounder of supermarket chain Grupo Mateus.
She and her then husband, Ilson Mateus, founded Grupo Mateus in 1986; he is the CEO and also a billionaire.
Brazil's fourth-largest food retailer, Grupo Mateus has 145 stores throughout the country's northern and northeastern regions.
The company, which employs 29,000 workers, went public in October 2020 in one of Brazil's largest IPOs of the year.
Ilson Mateus, who is a former gold miner, promised to use the $800 million raised in the IPO to double Grupo Mateus' workforce.
